story.text: 부산에 도착하자마자 향한 곳은 송도해상케이블카 매표소였다. 평일인데도 줄이 꽤 길었다. 용우는 익숙한 걸음으로 줄 맨 끝에 자리를 잡았다.
story.reading: bu-san-e do-chak-ha-ja-ma-ja hyang-han got-eun song-do-hae-sang-ke-i-beul-ka mae-pyo-so-yeot-da. pyeong-il-in-de-do jul-i kkwae gil-eot-da. yong-u-neun ig-suk-han geol-eum-eu-ro jul maen kkeut-e ja-ri-reul jab-at-da.
story.en: The moment we landed in Busan, we headed straight for the Songdo Marine Cable Car ticket booth. Even on a weekday, the line was long. Yongwoo settled into the back of it with an easy, familiar stride.

story.text: 누군가 슬쩍 새치기를 하려던 순간, 용우가 말없이 한 걸음 옆으로 움직여 자리를 막아섰다. 별다른 말도 없었는데 그 큰 체격 앞에서 남자는 슬그머니 뒤로 물러났다.
story.reading: nu-gun-ga seul-jjak sae-chi-gi-reul ha-ryeo-deon sun-gan, yong-u-ga mal-eop-si han geol-eum yeop-eu-ro um-jig-yeo ja-ri-reul mag-a-seot-da. byeol-da-reun mal-do eop-seon-neun-de geu keun che-gyeok ap-e-seo nam-ja-neun seul-geu-meo-ni dwi-ro mul-leo-nat-da.
story.en: The moment someone tried to slip into line ahead of us, Yongwoo silently shifted a step sideways, blocking the gap. He said nothing at all, but the man quietly backed off in front of that formidable build.

story.text: '질서는 지켜야지.' 그가 대수롭지 않게 중얼거렸다. 태권도로 다져진 자세 하나만으로 상황이 정리되는 걸 보며 나는 살짝 웃었다.
story.reading: jil-seo-neun ji-kyeo-ya-ji. geu-ga dae-su-rop-ji an-ke jung-eol-geo-ryeot-da. tae-kwon-do-ro da-jyeo-jin ja-se ha-na-man-eu-ro sang-hwang-i jeong-ni-doe-neun geol bo-myeo na-neun sal-jjak us-eot-da.
story.en: 'People should wait their turn.' He muttered it like it was nothing. Watching the situation resolve itself with just his taekwondo-honed posture, I couldn't help but smile a little.

story.text: 매표소 아저씨가 표를 건네며 무심코 물었다. '오빠야, 둘이요?' 부산 특유의 억양이었다. 용우가 별생각 없이 곧바로 대답했다. '예, 둘이요. 왕복으로 주이소.'
story.reading: mae-pyo-so a-jeo-ssi-ga pyo-reul geon-ne-myeo mu-sim-ko mul-eot-da. o-ppa-ya, dul-i-yo? bu-san teuk-yu-ui eog-yang-i-eot-da. yong-u-ga byeol-saeng-gak eop-si got-ba-ro dae-dab-aet-da. ye, dul-i-yo. wang-bog-eu-ro ju-i-so.
story.en: The man at the booth handed over the tickets, asking offhandedly, 'Just the two of you, bro?' — with that unmistakable Busan lilt. Without thinking, Yongwoo answered right back. 'Yeah, two of us. Round trip, please.'

story.text: 낯선 억양에 놀라 쳐다보자, 용우가 그제야 자기 말투를 눈치챈 듯 헛기침을 했다. '…어, 아니. 그, 여기 사투리가 옮았나 보다.' 서둘러 방송 멘트 같은 또박또박한 톤으로 돌아온다.
story.reading: nat-seon eog-yang-e nol-la chyeo-da-bo-ja, yong-u-ga geu-je-ya ja-gi mal-tu-reul nun-chi-chaen deut heot-gi-chim-eul haet-da. eo, a-ni. geu, yeo-gi sa-tu-ri-ga om-at-na bo-da. seo-dul-leo bang-song men-teu gat-eun tto-bak-tto-bak-an ton-eu-ro dol-a-on-da.
story.en: I turned to look, startled by the unfamiliar accent, and only then did Yongwoo seem to notice it himself, clearing his throat. '...Uh, no. Must've caught the local accent or something.' He hurried back into his usual crisp, radio-announcer cadence.

story.text: '옮았다'기엔 너무 자연스러웠다. 뭔가 캐묻고 싶었지만, 용우가 벌써 케이블카 쪽으로 성큼성큼 걸어가고 있었다.
story.reading: om-at-da-gi-en neo-mu ja-yeon-seu-reo-wot-da. mwon-ga kae-mut-go sip-eot-ji-man, yong-u-ga beol-sseo ke-i-beul-ka jjog-eu-ro seong-keum-seong-keum geol-eo-ga-go iss-eot-da.
story.en: That was far too smooth to be something he'd just 'caught.' I wanted to press him on it, but Yongwoo was already striding off toward the cable car.

story.text: '뭘 그렇게 봐. 케이블카 놓치겠다, 빨리 와.' 뒤도 안 돌아보고 재촉하는 목소리에 서둘러 따라나섰다. '가는 동안 대화나 들어봐라.'
story.reading: mwol geu-reo-ke bwa. ke-i-beul-ka noch-i-get-da, ppal-li wa. dwi-do an dol-a-bo-go jae-chok-ha-neun mok-so-ri-e seo-dul-leo tta-ra-na-seot-da. ga-neun dong-an dae-hwa-na deul-eo-bwa-ra.
story.en: 'What are you staring at. We'll miss the cable car, hurry up.' Not even turning around, he hurried me along, and I scrambled to catch up. 'Listen to some conversations on the way.'

words.example_en: He got dirty looks for cutting in line.

words.example: 그는 대수롭지 않다는 듯 어깨를 으쓱했다.
words.example_reading: geu-neun dae-su-rop-ji an-ta-neun deut eo-kkae-reul eu-sseuk-aet-da
words.example_en: He shrugged as if it were nothing much.
His accent gave away where he was from.

words.meaning: To be caught/transferred (a habit, an accent, an illness, etc.)
words.example_en: I guess I caught my friend's speech habit.
He hurried me along, saying we were late.

sentences.ko: 매표소 앞에 긴 줄이 늘어서 있었고, 용우는 익숙하게 줄 끝에 섰다.
sentences.reading: mae-pyo-so ap-e gin jul-i neul-eo-seo iss-eot-go, yong-u-neun ig-suk-ha-ge jul kkeut-e seot-da
sentences.en: A long line stretched in front of the ticket booth, and Yongwoo took his place at the end of it, at ease.

sentences.ko: 누군가 새치기를 하려 하자 그는 말없이 자리를 막아섰다.
sentences.reading: nu-gun-ga sae-chi-gi-reul ha-ryeo ha-ja geu-neun mal-eop-si ja-ri-reul mag-a-seot-da
sentences.en: When someone tried to cut in line, he silently blocked the spot.

sentences.ko: 매표소 직원의 사투리 섞인 말에 그는 대수롭지 않게 사투리로 답했다.
sentences.reading: mae-pyo-so jig-won-ui sa-tu-ri seokk-in mal-e geu-neun dae-su-rop-ji an-ke sa-tu-ri-ro dab-aet-da
sentences.en: In response to the booth clerk's dialect-tinged question, he answered back in dialect without a second thought.

sentences.ko: 낯선 억양을 눈치채고 놀라자 그는 사투리가 옮았다며 얼버무렸다.
sentences.reading: nat-seon eog-yang-eul nun-chi-chae-go nol-la-ja geu-neun sa-tu-ri-ga om-at-da-myeo eol-beo-mu-ryeot-da
sentences.en: When I looked startled at the unfamiliar accent, he brushed it off, saying he must've caught the local dialect.

sentences.ko: 그는 나를 재촉하며 케이블카 쪽으로 성큼성큼 걸어갔다.
sentences.reading: geu-neun na-reul jae-chok-ha-myeo ke-i-beul-ka jjog-eu-ro seong-keum-seong-keum geol-eo-gat-da
sentences.en: He hurried me along, striding briskly toward the cable car.

turns.speaker: 매표소 직원
turns.en: You two together? Should I do round trip?

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.en: Yeah, two of us. Round trip, please.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.en: ...You just spoke in dialect, didn't you?

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 무, 무슨 소리야. 잘못 들었다, 그거.
turns.reading: mu, mu-seun so-ri-ya. jal-mot deul-eot-da, geu-geo.
turns.en: Wh-what are you talking about. You must've misheard.

dialogues.question: 이 대화에서 용우가 사투리로 대답한 이유로 가장 알맞은 것은?
dialogues.question_en: What best explains why Yongwoo answered in dialect in this exchange?
options: 매표소 직원을 놀리려고 일부러 흉내 냈다
사투리를 배운 적이 있어서 연습해 본 것이다
dialogues.explanation: 용우는 부산이 고향이라, 방심한 순간 무의식중에 사투리가 튀어나왔습니다.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.text: 질서 지키라고 한마디만 했는데 그 사람이 왜 그렇게 순순히 물러났을까요?
turns.reading: jil-seo ji-ki-ra-go han-ma-di-man haen-neun-de geu sa-ram-i wae geu-reo-ke sun-sun-hi mul-leo-nass-eul-kka-yo?
turns.en: You only said one thing about keeping order — why did he back off so easily?

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 내가 좀, 그런 쪽으로 자세가 나오나 보다.
turns.reading: nae-ga jom, geu-reon jjog-eu-ro ja-se-ga na-o-na bo-da.
turns.en: I guess I've just got that kind of stance, in that department.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.text: 태권도 자세요? 그런 걸로 사람이 물러나요?
turns.reading: tae-kwon-do ja-se-yo? geu-reon geol-lo sa-ram-i mul-leo-na-yo?
turns.en: Your taekwondo stance? People back off from that?

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 국가대표 준비하던 게 어디 가겠냐. 몸이 먼저 기억하는 거지.
turns.reading: guk-ga-dae-pyo jun-bi-ha-deon ge eo-di ga-get-nya. mom-i meon-jeo gi-eok-a-neun geo-ji.
turns.en: Years of national-team training don't just disappear. My body remembers before I do.

dialogues.question: 새치기하던 사람이 순순히 물러난 이유로 가장 알맞은 것은?
dialogues.question_en: What best explains why the person trying to cut in line backed off so easily?
dialogues.correct_answer: 용우의 다부진 태권도 자세와 존재감에 위압감을 느껴서
options: 용우의 다부진 태권도 자세와 존재감에 위압감을 느껴서
dialogues.explanation: 용우는 별다른 말 없이도 태권도로 다져진 자세와 존재감만으로 상황을 정리했습니다.
